text:
sre-bot: Alert: token-slo-us-west-2 p99 TTFT breach (>=1200ms) for 10m. Affected: /v1/generate route. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/rtoken/token-slo?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2

alex: saw the alert, pulling up panels now. any immediate tails on tokens/sec or batching?

jess: tokens/sec spiked ~11:42 UTC on shard-7, continuous for ~8m. p50 stayed fine, p95 up ~600ms and p99 >1200ms. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/rtoken/token-slo?panelId=4

pranav: correlating with KV-cache miss rate. Prom query I ran: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, shard))
```
Shard-7 shows a clear jump. Also: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss[5m])) by (shard)` is 3x baseline.

maria: net metrics show small packet loss on node n-w-7a (0.8%) during the window, and retransmits up. Could be transient NIC or noisy neighbor on that host.

alex: so two hypotheses: (1) hotshard overload causing KV misses -> higher decode time, (2) network degradation impacting RPCs to kv-store. Need quick mitigation to reduce customer impact.

jess: immediate mitigations I can push: reduce max batch_size from 64 -> 32 for affected route, and route new requests off shard-7 (drain). Both are low-risk.

pranav: proposed commands to run: 
```bash
# drain shard-7 in routing layer
curl -s -XPOST "https://controlplane.redwood.internal/route/drain" -d '{"shard":"shard-7"}'

# reduce batching for route /v1/generate
curl -s -XPATCH "https://config.redwood.internal/routes/v1.generate" -d '{"batching.max_batch":32}'
```

maria: +1 for draining. I'll open a node-level ticket for n-w-7a and request NIC metrics + host reclamation. tagging infra-oncall.

tim: if we drain shard-7, we should verify capacity in nearby shards eu-west-1/ us-west-1 to accept shifted load. I see spare headroom in shard-3 and shard-4.

alex: jess, can you estimate cost delta if we scale up one extra GPU pool as warm standby? rough numbers for 1h please.

jess: quick back-of-envelope: spinning up one p4d-ish instance pool (equiv) for 1h = ~12% bump on hourly serving cost for region. If we do only routing + batch size change we should avoid that.

pranav: runbook I'm starting in the incident ticket: 1) drain shard-7, 2) reduce batching for /v1/generate, 3) monitor p99 and tokens/sec for 15m, 4) if p99 still > 800ms after 15m, trigger scale-up. I'll attach queries and dashboard snapshots.

alex: assigning tasks: pranav -> execute routing drain + runbook write; jess -> apply batch_size change & update Grafana alert thresholds (lower run length to 5m for more sensitivity), maria -> open host ticket and run NIC diagnostics, tim -> monitor downstream capacity and confirm acceptance.

maria: host ticket created: INC-2026 (n-w-7a). NIC diagnostics started (iperf + ethtool stats). Will update.

jess: batch_size patch applied, alert window shortened to 5m on the p99 rule (temporarily), and I added a new panel with per-shard tokens/sec heatmap. Link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/rtoken/token-slo?panelId=9

pranav: drain command returned 202, requests are rebalanced. Early telemetry: p99 dropped from ~1300ms -> ~640ms in the last 3m, tokens/sec stable.

alex: nice. keep the short mitigation for 30m then we can roll back batching change if host recovers. Also let's add an alert tweak: split p99 SLO by shard so we get noisy shard alerts instead of region-wide. jess can you add that to next sprint?

jess: will add a ticket for dashboard changes + alert split. PR later today.

tim: monitoring looks good. marking incident as mitigated for now, will keep an eye.

alex: thanks all. quick postmortem follow-ups: investigate KV cache eviction policy for hot keys, consider pre-warming or sticky-routing for high QPS prefixed tokens, and add a synthetic canary to detect hotshard/network combos earlier.

maria: noted for postmortem. INC-2026 will link to the postmortem doc.

pranav: closing the runbook section in the ticket. I'll keep the thread updated if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
